item.title: Café arábica atinge nova mínima em 10 semanas; açúcar bruto tem mínima em 2 semanas
item.description: Os contratos futuros do café arábica na bolsa ICE atingiram nesta quarta-feira uma nova mínima em dez semanas, devido às condições climáticas favoráveis no Brasil e ao aumento das exportações, enquanto o açúcar bruto atingiu uma mínima em duas semanas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do café arábica na bolsa ICE atingiram nesta quarta-feira uma nova mínima em dez semanas, devido às condições climáticas favoráveis no Brasil e ao aumento das exportações, enquanto o açúcar bruto atingiu uma mínima em duas semanas. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em baixa de 2,1 centavos, ou 0,7%, a US$2,8155 por libra-peso, após ter atingido uma mínima de dez semanas de US$2,7705 mais cedo. * "Os níveis de estoque da ICE permanecem baixos, mas o mercado está sendo pressionado por relatos de fortes exportações do Brasil e condições climáticas favoráveis ao cultivo para a safra de 2027", disse a corretora ADMIS. * Dados mostraram que as exportações de café verde do Brasil -- maior produtor mundial -- nas duas primeiras semanas de setembro registraram uma média diária de cerca de 13.500 toneladas métricas, um aumento de 51,5%. * No entanto, os estoques de café arábica da bolsa subiram para 233.479 sacas mais tarde na quarta-feira, com a divulgação do relatório diário da ICE, afastando-se da mínima de 27 anos de 217.646 sacas, segundo os dados. * A ICE informou que 16.210 sacas passaram pelas verificações de qualidade para entrar nos estoques certificados, enquanto 2.960 foram reprovadas. * O café robusta caiu 1,5%, para US$3.430 por tonelada métrica. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto apresentou pouca variação, cotado a 17,97 centavos por libra-peso, após ter atingido 17,68 -- seu nível mais baixo desde 3 de setembro -- mais cedo na sessão. * Os preços do petróleo recuaram, algo que geralmente incentiva as usinas de cana-de-açúcar no Brasil e na Índia a produzir mais açúcar e menos etanol, um biocombustível derivado da cana. * O açúcar perdeu terreno após a recente alta que o levou ao maior nível em 16 meses, mas permanece sustentado por possíveis quedas na produção na Índia, na União Europeia e na Tailândia, disseram operadores. * O tempo no Brasil deve ficar predominantemente seco nos próximos dez dias, permitindo a continuidade da colheita de cana-de-açúcar. * A França deve registrar sua menor colheita de beterraba açucareira desde a década de 1970, após ondas de calor e seca terem prejudicado as lavouras no maior produtor agrícola da UE, informou o Ministério da Agricultura. * O açúcar branco fechou em baixa de US$2,30, ou 0,4%, cotado a US$524,00 por tonelada. CACAU * O cacau em Londres fechou em alta de 63 libras, ou 1,5%, para 4.377 libras por tonelada. * Compradores de cacau em Gana -- o segundo maior produtor mundial -- têm cerca de 4 bilhões de cedis (US$349 milhões) a receber do órgão regulador referentes à safra passada e exigem o pagamento antes do início do novo ano-safra, disse uma entidade do setor à Reuters. * O volume de moagem de cacau na Costa do Marfim, um indicador de demanda, cresceu 21,3% em agosto na comparação anual, atingindo 47.646 toneladas métricas de amêndoas, segundo dados do setor do maior produtor mundial da commodity. * O cacau em Nova York subiu 0,9%, para US$5.979 por tonelada. (Reportagem de May Angel)

item.title: In rarity, Trump judicial nominee says US Capitol was attacked on January 6
item.description: A Kentucky state court judge nominated by President Donald Trump to a seat on the federal bench broke with the president's other judicial nominees on Wednesday by saying some rioters had been "attacking" the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A Kentucky state court judge nominated by President Donald Trump to a seat on the federal bench broke with the president's other judicial nominees on Wednesday by saying some rioters had been "attacking" the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. Daniel Ballou's frank description of what he saw on TV prompted five of Trump's other judicial nominees appearing beside him during a U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee hearing to distance themselves from his characterization of the actions of Trump's supporters at the Capitol that day. "I did not watch a lot of the coverage, but I did watch enough to see," Ballou said. "It certainly appeared like there were people attacking the Capitol. When you're slinging around barriers, breaking glass, and punching cops ... it appeared like some people were attacking the Capitol." Ballou, who was [USN:L1N44G0LR TEXT:"nominated"] by Trump to serve as a life-tenured judge on the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky, provided his views in response to a question from Democratic U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal. The Connecticut senator routinely at Senate Judiciary Committee hearings asks Trump's judicial nominees to answer who won the 2020 election and whether the Capitol was attacked by Trump's supporters. Those charged over the riot, a failed attempt to stop the congressional certification of Democrat Joe Biden's 2020 election victory, [USN:S0N3O6042 TEXT:"were later pardoned"] by Trump when he returned to office in January 2025. Like dozens of nominees to appear before the panel during Trump's second term, Ballou avoided stating who won the popular vote in 2020, saying only that Biden was "certified" the winner and declared the victor via the Electoral College. But when asked about the events of January 6, Ballou, who currently serves as chief circuit court judge in Kentucky's 34th Judicial Circuit, delivered an answer that Blumenthal said "strayed a little bit from the recitation that normally we find articulated." After Ballou spoke, Blumenthal pressed Richard Bennett, a magistrate judge nominated to serve as a district court judge in Texas's Southern District, for how he characterized the event. Bennett said he "saw some of the coverage and the violence, the vandalism and the trespass," which he condemned. "But characterizing it as an attack, I believe, weighs into a matter of political controversy, and it's inappropriate for me to comment on that under the canons," Bennett said. "Do the rest of you agree with Judge Ballou?" Blumenthal asked the four other nominees sitting beside Ballou and Bennett. "I agree with Judge Bennett, Senator," responded Courtney Coker, a prosecutor nominated to be a judge in Texas' Northern District. The other three nominees adopted Bennett's response. They were Trevor Pemberton, nominated to a judgeship in the Northern District of Oklahoma; Kyle Reardon, up for a position in Alaska; and Zachary West, who if confirmed by the Senate would serve as judge in the Eastern District of Oklahoma. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Ruído de data centers surge como risco crescente para seguradoras
item.description: Reclamações relacionadas ao ruído no entorno de data centers estão se tornando cada vez mais um risco potencial de responsabilidade civil para as seguradoras, já que a rápida construção próxima a comunidades residenciais gera litígios e um maior escrutínio das coberturas existentes, afirmou Cameron Douglass, diretor regional do grupo de prática ambiental da Gallagher, ao programa The Insurer TV.
item.dc:creator: Isha Marathe
item.content:encoded: Reclamações relacionadas ao ruído no entorno de data centers estão se tornando cada vez mais um risco potencial de responsabilidade civil para as seguradoras, já que a rápida construção próxima a comunidades residenciais gera litígios e um maior escrutínio das coberturas existentes, afirmou Cameron Douglass, diretor regional do grupo de prática ambiental da Gallagher, ao programa The Insurer TV. Segundo Douglass, o ruído deixou de ser associado principalmente às atividades de construção para se tornar uma preocupação operacional. Uma razão para essa mudança é que os data centers de maior porte, incluindo os de hiperescala, exigem mais equipamentos de refrigeração, geração de energia de reserva e outras infraestruturas que são mais barulhentas do que os campi tradicionais. “As reclamações estão se tornando mais organizadas; elas estão atraindo a atenção do meio jurídico”, disse Douglass à The Insurer TV. “Certamente isso será cada vez mais tratado como um risco potencial de responsabilidade civil, em vez de apenas um incômodo.” A tendência também está gerando dúvidas sobre quais apólices cobririam essas reclamações. Historicamente, o ruído tem sido visto sob a ótica da responsabilidade civil comercial geral, disse Douglass, mas algumas seguradoras de sinistros estão começando a lidar com essa exposição por meio de exclusões, franquias mais altas ou sublimites. As seguradoras ambientais, por sua vez, consideram cada vez mais os riscos relacionados a incômodos, incluindo odores, vibração e luz, embora a cobertura explícita para ruído ainda não seja generalizada. “Se uma apólice de responsabilidade civil geral contiver limitações relacionadas à poluição… e uma apólice ambiental não abordar expressamente o ruído, então o segurado poderá se ver diante dessa complicada discussão sobre cobertura”, disse Douglass. A Gallagher está discutindo a cobertura expressa contra ruído com seguradoras ambientais à medida que o risco se instala. Douglass disse que as seguradoras estão cada vez mais analisando fatores como proximidade de comunidades residenciais, reclamações existentes, requisitos de zoneamento, estudos acústicos e medidas de mitigação de ruído. Embora ainda seja cedo para avaliar o panorama das reclamações relacionadas ao ruído decorrentes de data centers, ele observou que múltiplas ações judiciais semelhantes em instalações que utilizam equipamentos ou práticas operacionais comuns poderiam, eventualmente, gerar preocupações de agregação para as seguradoras.

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold out for Week 2
item.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold was ruled out for Week 2 with a hip injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold was ruled out for Week 2 with a hip injury. Darnold is not being placed on injured reserve, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Wednesday, but will be relegated to rehab work for the next several days. That means Drew Lock will start for Seattle against the Arizona Cardinals with Jalen Milroe serving as the No. 2 quarterback. A timeframe for Darnold's return to practice hasn't been shared but Macdonald reiterated there is no cause or reason to "shut down" Darnold from physical activity. "He's killing it on his rehab. He's doing a lot," Macdonald said. Lock came off the bench in the first quarter of the midweek opener to lead the Seahawks to a victory over the Patriots. Seattle intercepted Drake Maye three times, including a game-sealing pick in the end zone on New England's final drive. The Seahawks haven't considered adding a quarterback. But Darnold's progress or any potential setback could change things. "We'll reevaluate every day, reevaluate next week and go from there," Macdonald said. Darnold led Seattle to a Super Bowl title last season in his first year with the team. --Field Level Media

item.title: Canada applies to join UK-led military coalition
item.description: Canada, seeking to diversify its defense ties away from the United States, has formally applied to join the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force military coalition, Prime Minister Mark Carney's office said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada, seeking to diversify its defense ties away from the United States, has formally applied to join the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force military coalition, Prime Minister Mark Carney's office said on Wednesday. The force, a grouping of 10 North Atlantic NATO member states, is a rapid response military partnership. "Prime Minister Carney announced that Canada has formally applied to join the Joint Expeditionary Force and welcomed the UK's support for Canada's participation in this important initiative," Carney's office said in a statement. Canada, already a member of NATO, is seeking closer military cooperation with European nations as it tries to reduce its reliance on the United States. Carney had earlier met British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in northern England. The two men discussed opportunities for defense industrial cooperation through the Global Combat Air Programme, an advanced fighter jet project that Canada [USN:L1N43H0Z9 TEXT:"joined"] as an observer in July 2026, Carney's office said. The JEF comprises Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom.

item.title: Soja sobe em Chicago enquanto operadores aguardam encontro entre Trump e Xi
item.description: Os futuros da soja na bolsa de Chicago subiram nesta quarta-feira e atingiram máximas do contrato nos meses mais distantes, impulsionados pelas expectativas de aumento da demanda chinesa.
item.dc:creator: Tom Polansek
item.content:encoded: Os futuros da soja na bolsa de Chicago subiram nesta quarta-feira e atingiram máximas do contrato nos meses mais distantes, impulsionados pelas expectativas de aumento da demanda chinesa. Os futuros de farelo de soja também atingiram máximas do contrato. Os operadores aguardavam para ver se a China, principal importadora, aumentaria as compras de soja dos Estados Unidos durante uma reunião prevista entre os presidentes Donald Trump e Xi Jinping em Washington na próxima semana. Na terça-feira, o secretário do Treasury dos EUA, Scott Bessent, divulgou planos para se reunir com seu homólogo chinês neste fim de semana. As especulações sobre a demanda global também ajudaram a sustentar os preços do farelo de soja. "O movimento mais surpreendente está ocorrendo no farelo, onde novas máximas são constantes, assim como os aumentos nos contratos em aberto, com rumores de que a demanda por exportações está se recuperando", disse Charlie Sernatinger, vice-presidente executivo da Marex. Os futuros de soja mais negociados fecharam em alta de 1,75 centavo, a US$13,205 por bushel. Os futuros de farelo de soja encerraram com alta de US$0,20, a US$365,60 por tonelada curta, após terem subido anteriormente para uma máxima de US$368,70. Os futuros de trigo também avançaram na CBOT, com o contrato mais negociado fechando em alta de 2,25 centavos, a US$7,3075 por bushel. Mas os futuros de milho encerraram em queda de 1,50 centavo, a US$5,3425 por bushel, enquanto os operadores aguardavam os resultados da colheita nos EUA.

item.title: OpenAI, Microsoft fend off part of software developer lawsuit over AI training
item.description: A U.S. appeals court on Wednesday upheld a win for OpenAI and its largest financial backer Microsoft , against part of a lawsuit brought by software developers who said the companies misused code stored on the Microsoft-owned software platform GitHub to train generative AI systems.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A U.S. appeals court on Wednesday upheld a win for OpenAI and its largest financial backer Microsoft (MSFT.O) , against part of a lawsuit brought by software developers who said the companies misused code stored on the Microsoft-owned software platform GitHub to train generative AI systems. The San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a California judge's ruling that OpenAI and Microsoft could not be held liable for violating the developers' rights under a U.S. copyright law. Attorneys for the developers and spokespeople for OpenAI and Microsoft did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the ruling. Two anonymous plaintiffs, seeking to represent a class of people who own open-source code published on GitHub, sued Microsoft and OpenAI in 2022. They said the companies trained OpenAI's Codex and Microsoft's Copilot AI coding tools with code from GitHub repositories in violation of a federal copyright law — the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) — and open-source licensing terms. The DMCA bars the removal of copyright management information (CMI) from copyrighted works. CMI is identifying information about a work such as its author and copyright owner. The developers alleged that the companies violate the DMCA when Codex and Copilot reproduce their code without attributing it to them. The lawsuit was one of the first in a [USN:L6N3XM122 TEXT:"wave of high-stakes cases"] brought by copyright owners including authors, news outlets and music labels against tech companies over the use of their material in AI training. Most of those cases focus on copyright infringement claims, unlike the software developers' case. U.S. District Judge Jon Tigar dismissed the developers' DMCA claim, but allowed the developers to continue pressing claims that OpenAI and Microsoft violated open-source licensing terms. The 9th Circuit upheld the dismissal of the DMCA claims on Wednesday after finding Copilot and Codex do not remove copyright information from existing works, but instead generate new works that never contained such information. Copyright claims concerning an AI system's output are often based on traditional infringement principles. The appeals court on Wednesday differentiated DMCA claims from infringement claims, which require a showing that the output is "substantially similar" to the copyrighted work at issue. If substantial similarity was "all it took" to violate the DMCA, the statute would "supplant traditional copyright protections and subject defendants to potentially ruinous liability under the DMCA’s enhanced statutory damages," the appeals court said. The court added that it was not deciding whether similarities between AI-generated code and copyrighted code could support a copyright infringement claim. The case is Doe v. GitHub Inc, 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 24-7700. For the developers: Jesse Panuccio of Boies Schiller Flexner For OpenAI and Microsoft: Lisa Blatt of Williams & Connolly; and Christopher Cariello of Orrick Herrington & Sutcliffe Read more: [USN:L1N34C14M TEXT:"OpenAI, Microsoft want court to toss lawsuit accusing them of abusing open-source code"]

item.title: Netanyahu steps up threats against directors of Gaza documentary 'NAZA'
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Wednesday to pass a law to revoke the citizenship of anyone who defames Israel's soldiers, his latest threat against the Israeli directors of "NAZA", a documentary about soldiers' killing of Gaza civilians.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Wednesday to pass a law to revoke the citizenship of anyone who defames Israel's soldiers, his [USN:L1N4560KT TEXT:"latest threat"] against the Israeli directors of "NAZA", a documentary about soldiers' killing of Gaza civilians. Directed by Israeli journalists Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, [USN:L8N4520QP TEXT:"NAZA"] alleges that mass civilian deaths were routinely built into Israeli targeting decisions in Gaza, something Netanyahu and the military reject. The film, which won a major prize at the Venice Film Festival on Saturday, takes its title from an Israeli military term for expected "collateral casualties" and is built around anonymous interviews with intelligence officers and soldiers. It has drawn a backlash in Israel, with the military examining potential legal action against those involved in it. But it has also played into the charged political atmosphere ahead of Israel's October 27 election, which public opinion polls show Netanyahu's right-wing coalition could lose. On Tuesday, Netanyahu accused some of his election rivals of failing to take a tough stand against the documentary, saying this made them unfit for office. And on Wednesday, he pledged to advance two bills that he said aimed at addressing the "immense damage" done to Israeli soldiers. "The first, to revoke the citizenship of anyone who defames (Israeli) soldiers, and the second to hit them in their pockets and increase the statutory damages for defamation they can be sued for by 20 times," Netanyahu said in a social media video. "We will hit them both in their pockets and in their citizenship, as their place is not with us." Netanyahu cited three incidents in proposing the bills: "the recent film NAZA which portrayed (Israeli) officers and soldiers as war criminals"; 2025 remarks by left-wing ex-general turned politician Yair Golan that "a sane country does not kill children as a hobby"; and a military legal officer's 2024 [USN:L1N3WC0N7 TEXT:"leak"] of a video showing soldiers abusing a Gaza detainee. Reuters could not immediately reach the NAZA filmmakers for comment. In 2022, Israel's Supreme Court [USN:L8N2Z25AB TEXT:"upheld a law"] that permits stripping citizenship from Israelis who carry out actions that constitute a breach of trust against the state. Any new legislation would likely face similar court challenges. The NAZA filmmakers say they believe it is important that Israelis watch the documentary and grapple with the narrative it presents. Gaza health authorities say more than 73,000 Palestinians, most of them civilians, have been killed in Israel's military campaign that has left much of Gaza in ruins. The war was triggered by Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack on Israel which killed 1,200 people, most of them civilians, according to Israeli tallies.

item.title: US DFC approves €85 million loan to Ukraine's DTEK
item.description: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation approved an €85 million ($97.5 million) loan to Ukraine's largest private energy company, DTEK, to expand its battery storage, DFC and DTEK said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. [USN:L1N4580LW TEXT:"International Development Finance Corporation"] approved an €85 million ($97.5 million) loan to Ukraine's largest private energy company, DTEK, to expand its battery storage, DFC and DTEK said on Wednesday. It is the DFC's largest loan for Ukraine's energy sector since the start of Russia's invasion in 2022. "This €85 million loan means we can release more funds to build more battery storage and other projects," said Maxim Timchenko, the chief executive officer of DTEK. "For me, the financial part is very important, but much more significant is this signal that DFC is ready to support Ukraine and DTEK." "They have made an assessment of the risk, understand how to manage it, and are saying that private investors should follow," he said. DFC's chief executive, Ben Black, said in a statement that U.S. President Donald Trump had empowered the DFC to proceed with the investment. "These projects will support billions in American exports, secure critical infrastructure and resources in Ukraine, Jordan, Central Asia, and across Africa, and strengthen U.S. companies competing in some of the most important markets in the world.” DTEK is owned by SCM Holdings, whose sole shareholder and ultimate beneficiary is Rinat Akhmetov, Ukraine's richest man. Last year, DTEK launched Ukraine's largest battery storage facility to ensure stable power supplies as Russia has persistently targeted Ukrainian energy facilities in missile and drone attacks during more than four years of war. Six battery storage systems have been connected to the power grid in the capital, Kyiv, and in Dnipropetrovsk region in Eastern Ukraine. The facilities, constructed in partnership with U.S.-based Fluence (FLNC.O) , a battery storage technology company, have the capacity to store 400 megawatt hours of electricity — enough to power 600,000 Ukrainian households for two hours. ($1 = 0.8721 euro)

item.title: ＡＩ規制は不要、懸念あおるのは「常とう手段」＝サックス米大統領顧問
item.description:
Courtney Rozen
[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Courtney Rozen

[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領の外部技術顧問デービッド・サックス氏は１６日、人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る国民の懸念は、ＡＩ規制を求める活動やメディアの報道によってあおられているとの見解を示した。今週初め、ＡＩへの新たな規制を求める声を一蹴したトランプ氏の発言に同調する形となった。

サックス氏はワシントンで開かれたポリティコのイベントにビデオで登場し、ＡＩ開発企業は自社製品の安全性確保に責任を負うべきであり、問題が生じた場合は「法的責任」を問われることになると指摘。その上で、新たな規制は必要ないとの考えを示した。

また同氏は、ＡＩが米国社会に与える影響への懸念に言及し、「われわれはこうした恐怖をあおる常とう手段を何度も目にしてきた」と述べた。

ＡＩの潜在的脅威への警戒感は先週、アンソロピックの研究者ジェイコブ・コクソン氏が退社を表明し、「ＡＩを構築している人々は、ＡＩが今後１０年以内にわれわれ全員を殺す可能性があると本気で信じている」と述べたことで一段と強まった。

こうした中、トランプ大統領は１４日、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、ＡＩ開発に疑念が投げかけられることで、中国が利益を得ることになるとの考えを示し、「ＡＩに必要な唯一の管理や『ガードレール』は、強く聡明な（高ＩＱの）大統領だ。米国にはそれが十分にある」と述べた。

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル上昇、ＦＲＢが3年超ぶり利上げ 追加引き締め見通しも
item.description: ［ニューヨーク １６日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが主要通貨バスケットに対して上昇した。米連邦準備理...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル上昇、ＦＲＢが3年超ぶり利上げ　追加引き締め見通しも 5:30 配信

2024年2月、ナイロビで撮影。REUTERS/Thomas Mukoya

［ニューヨーク　１６日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが主要通貨バスケットに対して上昇した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による３年超ぶりの利上げと追加利上げ見通しが材料視された。

ＦＲＢは１５─１６日に開いた連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で、フェデラルファンド（ＦＦ）金利誘導目標を０．２５％ポイント引き上げ、３．７５─４．００％とすることを決定した。決定は全会一致だった。

ＦＯＭＣに合わせて公表された最新の金利・経済見通しでは、１８人の政策当局者のうち１６人が年内に少なくともあと１回、０．２５％ポイントの利上げが必要になると予想。現在の金利水準が維持されると見込んだのは２人にとどまった。ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長は前回６月に続き、見通しの公表を見送った。

コーペイのチーフマーケットストラテジスト、カール・シャモッタ氏は、全会一致での利上げ決定と金利見通しの上方修正について、「インフレ抑制に向けたＦＲＢの取り組みに対する信認の回復につながり、ドル相場の重しとなっていた要因を取り除くことになるだろう」と述べた。

主要通貨に対するドル指数＜＝USD＞は０．３％高の９９．９６１と、約５週間ぶりの高値を付けた。

ユーロ／ドルは０．３％安の１．１５０２ドル、ポンド／ドルは０．５％安の１．３４１５５ドル。

イングランド銀行（英中銀）は１７日に金融政策決定会合を開く。市場では据え置き観測が優勢となっている。

ドル／円は０．３％高の１５５．４９円。

日銀も１７─１８日に金融政策決定会合を開く。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、トレーダーは日銀が８０％の確率で利上げを実施すると見込んでいる。また、来年１月末までに０．２５％ポイントの利上げが２回実施されるとの見方も織り込まれている。

ジュリアス・ベアのエコノミスト、デビッド・Ａ・マイヤー氏は「円相場は今後も金利差に大きく左右されるだろう」と指摘。「われわれは最近、ドル／円相場の見通しを１５５円に修正した。これは、日銀が現在市場に織り込まれている引き締めペースを最終的に実現できるかどうかについて、一部で懐疑的な見方があることを反映している」と述べた。

暗号資産（仮想通貨）市場では、ビットコインはほぼ横ばいの７万５８０９ドル。１５日には、米上院がトランプ大統領の支持する包括的な暗号資産関連法案の審議入りを否決したことを受け、４％下落していた。

item.title: Banks provide $22 billion chip loan to Blackstone, Alphabet cloud venture, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: A group of 10 banks is providing a $22 billion chip loan to support Blackstone and Alphabet's new cloud venture Crux AI, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A group of 10 banks is providing a $22 billion chip loan to support Blackstone (BX.N) and Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) new cloud venture Crux AI, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter. The banks include Goldman Sachs Group (GS.N) , Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp, Barclays (BARC.L) , BNP Paribas SA and Bank of Nova Scotia (BNS.TO) , the report said. Google and Blackstone [USN:L6N41W00W TEXT:"announced"] the venture in May, saying they would form a cloud business aimed at meeting growing demand for AI computing services. Blackstone would invest an initial $5 billion in equity to help bring 500 megawatts of data center capacity online in 2027, with further expansion planned. The venture comes as tech companies ramp up spending on data centers, power and specialized chips to support AI applications. The debt will be used to purchase Google's custom Tensor Processing Units, and will be backed by the value of those chips and Crux AI's customer contracts, according to the report. Blackstone, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, BNP, Barclays, Bank of Nova Scotia, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

item.title: Ravens place rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens placed rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane on injured reserve on Wednesday after he had wrist surgery.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Ravens placed rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane on injured reserve on Wednesday after he had wrist surgery. In a corresponding move, the Ravens promoted veteran wide receiver Chris Moore from the practice squad to the 53-man roster. Star wide receiver Zay Flowers missed practice on Wednesday because of a hamstring injury sustained in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the host Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Head coach Jesse Minter said Flowers' status is day-to-day. Lane, 22, will be out a minimum of four games, and Minter said that the rookie "definitely has a really good chance of coming back here pretty quick." Baltimore selected Lane in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Southern California. Lane caught one of his three targets for 11 yards in his NFL debut before the injury on Sunday. Moore had one catch on two targets for 53 yards in Sunday's game. The 33-year-old has 150 career receptions for 1,970 yards and nine touchdowns in 126 regular-season games (23 starts) over parts of 11 seasons with the Ravens (2016-20), Houston Texans (2021-22), Tennessee Titans (2023), Arizona Cardinals (2024), Washington Commanders (2024-25) and Ravens. The Ravens picked Moore in the fourth round of the 2016 draft out of Cincinnati. Flowers, 26, had five receptions on six targets for 150 yards and one touchdown on Sunday before exiting in the second quarter. Baltimore selected Flowers 22nd overall in the 2023 draft out of Boston College. He was voted to the Pro Bowl in 2024 and 2025. The Ravens filled Moore's spot on the practice roster with veteran cornerback Amani Oruwriye, 30, who played in one game for the team in 2025. He has played in 62 games (40) starts in the league since 2019. Baltimore hosts the New Orleans Saints (0-1) on Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Everyone wants safer AI. But who will rein it in?
item.description: Even for someone who has spent the past decade covering this fast-moving industry, the past week felt extraordinary: researchers warning about human extinction, followed by AI lab CEOs urging a coordinated slowdown; capped by a president calling all the alarmism a hoax.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Even for someone who has spent the past decade covering this fast-moving industry, the past week felt extraordinary: researchers warning about human extinction, followed by AI lab CEOs urging a coordinated slowdown; capped by a president calling all the alarmism a hoax. If you’re wondering how we got from hallucinating chatbots to conversations about human extinction, my colleague Aditya Soni has a [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"useful explainer"]. One reason is the rapid progress in recursive self-learning, techniques that allow models to improve by training on their own outputs, which some researchers say has accelerated capabilities too fast for alignment and safety work to keep up. Recent incidents have also made those risks feel less theoretical. Our [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"reporting"] on OpenAI agents attacking Hugging Face showed how autonomous agents can operate in swarms, cover their tracks and pursue a goal while creating unintended consequences along the way. Now, remarkably, the biggest frontier labs appear to agree on at least one thing: the pace itself may need to slow. But what would a slowdown actually look like and who has agreed to it? This week, we take you inside Salesforce’s annual Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, where what is usually a giant marketing spectacle turned into a live debate over AI safety and control. Scroll on. Do you think AI labs need regulations to slow down? Share your thoughts by emailing me or following me on LinkedIn . Forward this newsletter to your friend who would benefit from weekly news and insights on AI. They can also subscribe here . OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI: [USN:L8N45601P TEXT:"How China is preparing for the risk of AI escaping human control"] [USN:L4N4530HO TEXT:"SK Hynix, Intel in talks about deal to make memory chips in US"] [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"OpenAI's rogue agents probed Hugging Face for weaknesses two months before major hack"] [USN:L6N45316U TEXT:"Nvidia in talks to invest in Anthropic’s mega IPO"] [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"From hallucinating AI chatbots to wiping out humanity - How we got here"] AI REGULATION? DEPENDS ON WHO YOU ASK By Aditya Soni & Krystal Hu , Technology Correspondents With the AI safety debate simmering, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff turned this year’s Dreamforce, ostensibly a giant conference about how enterprises can harness AI, into a livestreamed stage for a more consequential argument: Who decides how fast frontier AI is allowed to move? Within hours of one another, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman took the stage in San Francisco and offered three different answers. Speaking to roughly 10,000 people in the room and about 10 times that online, Amodei laid out the three-step plan from a 3,800-word essay he published over the weekend: Anthropic should improve its own safety practices, leading AI companies should agree on shared standards, and those standards should eventually underpin some kind of international regulatory mechanism. “Obviously, it’s very tempting to attack your competitor and say these guys are unsafe,” said Amodei, whose company is expected to go public in weeks as we [USN:L6N45316U TEXT:"reported"]. A better place to start, he argued, was for companies to examine their own records, recommit to transparency and spend more on safety. Anthropic is working on that first step, he said, and plans to open a dialogue with rivals on the rest. Then came Jensen Huang, with almost the opposite prescription. Standing beside the 6-foot-5 Benioff, Huang joked that he wished someone would bring him a chair to stand on. But on regulation, he was unequivocal. Companies already have incentives to pace themselves until they are confident a product is safe and useful, he argued. “We don’t need any new laws,” Huang said. The idea that the industry must choose between innovation, speed and safety, he argued, is a false one. Hours later, Altman landed somewhere in between. The world is right to fear AI, he said, even as he argued that the technology can be developed safely. Some accidents are inevitable with a powerful new technology, Altman said, pointing to aviation: Planes became safer not because crashes disappeared, but because incidents were investigated, reported and used to change standards. Companies should be willing “to slow down or stop” if they reach a point where they cannot proceed safely, he said. But the aviation analogy also points to something larger than corporate judgment alone: a system of independent oversight capable of learning from failures and setting rules across an industry. So after listening to all three, the divide seemed less about whether AI needs guardrails than about who should hold the brake. The most tangible progress to come out of the AI safety debate has been the use of third-party evaluators with deeper access to frontier models at OpenAI and Anthropic, so external researchers can test increasingly powerful systems and provide independent checks. But it is unclear what authority those evaluators would have to tell frontier labs, with billions on the line, that they have to go back to the drawing board and delay releasing models. That’s especially true at a time when the gap between open-source and frontier models is closing. Washington appears unwilling to play a role here. The Trump administration’s current framework explicitly opposes creating a new federal AI rulemaking agency, while emphasizing the need to avoid unnecessary barriers to development. “We're leading China in AI…frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins,” Trump told Huang on a call on stage at the AII-In Summit this week. Huang believes companies have commercial and legal incentives that prevent them from releasing dangerous products. Over-regulation could also stymie burgeoning U.S. open-source development. That is particularly important to Nvidia’s business because a broad ecosystem of competing model developers helps to sustain demand across its customer base while providing an alternative to powerful Chinese open-source models. Companies also have to make business decisions — especially when trillion-dollar IPOs and enormous funding rounds are at stake. When resources are finite, do you spend them on another powerful training run or a more capable product, or do you divert some of them into expensive safety research with a commercial payoff that may be less immediate? Recent AI-agent incidents, which my colleagues have reported on extensively, also expose a more alarming observation in this unregulated new frontier: What if the developers themselves do not fully understand what their systems are capable of? The discovery of rogue AI activity was first uncovered by the victim, Hugging Face, and not the perpetrator, OpenAI. Outside researchers later uncovered [USN:L6N44W08B TEXT:"more unreported activities"]. In the RubyGems case, people familiar with the matter told Reuters that OpenAI employees realized their own agents were responsible only after outside researchers identified them. Self-regulation therefore rests on two assumptions: that companies want to restrain their systems when necessary, and that they reliably can. The recent debate suggests neither can be taken for granted — even if the companies start with the best intentions. CHART OF THE WEEK Americans who already use AI regularly are becoming slightly less trusting of the technology. But the real shift is among the skeptics: people who rarely or never use AI are becoming far more distrustful. A Gallup survey released this week found that 43% of people who use AI at least sometimes said they trust it, down from 46% a year earlier. Among people who rarely or never use AI, trust fell much more sharply, to 12% from last year’s 23%. That widening gap matters as AI companies push their products deeper into work, healthcare, education and everyday life. AI skeptics are becoming significantly harder to win over. It’s also worth noting that the survey was conducted in June, before the recent wave of rogue AI incidents and the warnings from researchers and executives about AI posing catastrophic risks.

item.title: CDC delay holds up children's COVID vaccine orders, WSJ reports
item.description: U.S. states are facing delays in obtaining COVID-19 vaccines for children through a federal immunization program, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. states are facing delays in obtaining COVID-19 vaccines for children through a federal immunization program, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has not started accepting orders for COVID-19 shots, according to the report. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The holdup comes as the Trump administration scales back vaccine guidance. The CDC no longer recommends that all children get a COVID shot and is instead urging parents to consult their doctors. A federal judge earlier this year blocked the administration from enacting a narrower vaccine schedule. Vaccine hesitancy is rising nationwide, and measles outbreaks are spreading, with four measles-related deaths being reported in Pennsylvania earlier on Tuesday. Demand for COVID booster shots has already fallen sharply, and fewer than 10% of children aged six months to 17 were vaccinated last year, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing CDC data.

item.title: Confianza de constructores de viviendas EEUU cae en septiembre a mínimo en 12 meses
item.description: La confianza de los constructores de viviendas de Estados Unidos cayó en septiembre a su nivel más bajo en un año, ya que el aumento de las tasas hipotecarias frenó la demanda de casas, reveló una encuesta publicada el miércoles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La confianza de los constructores de viviendas de Estados Unidos cayó en septiembre a su nivel más bajo en un año, ya que el aumento de las tasas hipotecarias frenó la demanda de casas, reveló una encuesta publicada el miércoles. El índice del mercado inmobiliario de la Asociación Nacional de Constructores de Viviendas (NAHB) y Wells Fargo bajó tres puntos este mes a 32, el valor más bajo desde septiembre de 2025, frente a los 35 registrados en agosto. Este descenso también refleja la escasez de mano de obra, en un contexto de medidas más estrictas contra la inmigración, así como el aumento de los costos debido a los aranceles sobre las importaciones. Los economistas encuestados por Reuters habían pronosticado que el índice bajaría a 34. Es probable que la confianza se mantenga contenida en los próximos meses, ya que las tasas hipotecarias han ido subiendo al mismo ritmo que el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años. La tasa de interés hipotecaria fija a 30 años se situó en promedio en el 6,76% la semana pasada, el nivel más alto en más de un año, frente al 6,71% de la semana anterior, según datos de la entidad hipotecaria Freddie Mac. El rendimiento de los bonos a 10 años alcanzó el martes el 5,041%, el nivel más alto desde julio de 2007, impulsado en parte por las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal comenzara el miércoles a subir las tasas de interés para frenar la inflación, impulsada por la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán. Los retornos a más largo plazo también han subido en medio de la preocupación por el creciente endeudamiento del país. "La afluencia de compradores se ha debilitado en gran parte del país, debido en gran medida al aumento de las tasas hipotecarias", dijo Bill Owens, presidente de la NAHB. "Los constructores también siguen enfrentándose a unos costos de materiales más elevados, al aumento de los precios de la gasolina y el diésel y a una persistente escasez de mano de obra. En algunos mercados, los constructores informan de que el endurecimiento de las medidas de control de la inmigración está disuadiendo a los trabajadores legales de acudir a las obras". El aumento de los costos de financiación y los precios de la vivienda, que siguen siendo elevados, están haciendo que los potenciales compradores se mantengan al margen. La Asociación Nacional de Agentes Inmobiliarios informó la semana pasada de que las ventas de viviendas de segunda mano cayeron en agosto a su nivel más bajo en 14 meses. Además, existe un exceso de viviendas nuevas sin vender en el mercado, lo que disuade a los constructores de iniciar nuevos proyectos. El porcentaje de constructores que afirman haber rebajado los precios aumentó este mes al 38%, frente al 35% registrado en agosto. La reducción promedio de los precios se mantuvo sin cambios en el 6% por sexto mes consecutivo. El uso de incentivos de venta subió al 66%, frente al 63% de agosto. El indicador de la encuesta sobre las condiciones actuales de venta bajó cuatro puntos a 35, mientras que el indicador de las ventas futuras se desplomó seis puntos a 37. El indicador del flujo de compradores potenciales se mantuvo sin cambios en 23.

item.title: Federalist Society and University of Austin team up for new law program
item.description: The University of Austin — a five-year-old Texas institution that bills itself as an oasis of free speech and academic freedom in U.S. higher education — is working with the conservative Federalist Society to launch an undergraduate law program that leaders hope to expand into a law school after receiving an $11 million donation, its president told Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: The University of Austin — a five-year-old Texas institution that bills itself as an oasis of free speech and academic freedom in U.S. higher education — is working with the conservative Federalist Society to launch an undergraduate law program that leaders hope to expand into a law school after receiving an $11 million donation, its president told Reuters on Wednesday. University president Carlos Carvalho said the influential lawyer association, which has chapters at many U.S. law schools, will help develop a law curriculum that emphasizes the Constitution, rules, and individual liberty. “The connection to the Federalist Society is an important one,” he said. UATX, as the tuition-free university is known, opened to students in 2024 and says it makes admissions decisions based on merit alone. Its founding trustees include Bari Weiss, founder of the Free Press news website and the editor-in-chief of CBS News since last year, and Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale. The Federalist Society did not respond to a request for comment Wednesday on its role in the new law program. It will prepare students to be admitted to top law schools by offering rigorous legal training in their upper-class years and opportunities for hands-on legal training, Carvalho said. He said a law school offering a J.D.— the university does not yet have any graduate programs — could launch as soon as 2028, though he called that timeline “aggressive.” Carvalho and Federalist Society President Sheldon Gilbert unveiled the donation and plans during a Constitution Day address on Tuesday featuring federal appeals court judge James Ho. The judge in 2022 said he would [USN:L1N3661YU TEXT:"not hire"] Yale Law School graduates as clerks in protest of “cancel culture” and an intolerance of conservative viewpoints. He later extended his clerk boycott to graduates of the law schools at Stanford and Columbia. The $11 million donation is from Gail Jaquish, founder of behavioral research firm Jurix Inc., and her husband Steven Kenninger, founder of private investment firm QMO. Kenninger is a Stanford Law School alum. The couple did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Wednesday through their foundation. Carvalho said recent changes to Texas’ attorney licensing rules were among the factors that motivated UATX to add law to its undergraduate offerings and look at adding a law school. The Texas Supreme Court earlier this year [USN:L6N3Y80WI TEXT:"ended its reliance"] on the American Bar Association for law school accreditation and instead established its own list of law schools whose graduates may practice in the state. Carvalho said that change could make it easier for graduates of a future UATX law school to become licensed. Read more: [USN:L6N3Y80WI TEXT:"Texas becomes first state to end ABA role in lawyer admissions"] [USN:L1N3661YU TEXT:"Conservative judges extend clerk boycott to Stanford after disrupted speech"] Additional reporting by Nate Raymond

item.title: US appeals court questions Trump attempts to dismantle three agencies
item.description: A federal appeals court on Wednesday appeared unlikely to allow President Donald Trump's administration to dismantle three small federal agencies by firing most of their employees and terminating grants.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court on Wednesday appeared unlikely to allow President Donald Trump's administration to dismantle three small federal agencies by firing most of their employees and terminating grants. A U.S. Department of Justice lawyer during arguments told the Boston-based 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals that a lower-court judge had wrongly blocked the administration's actions affecting the Minority Business Development Agency, the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service and the U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness. "The upshot is that the current administration is left with the policy choices about the appropriate size and scope of three federal agencies frozen in amber, unable to change those at the president's direction," said Justice Department attorney Simon Jerome. The agencies were all targeted by Trump in an executive order he signed in March 2025 that called for "reduction in the elements of the Federal bureaucracy that the President has determined are unnecessary." Jerome argued that U.S. District Judge John McConnell in Rhode Island lacked jurisdiction to issue an injunction because the agencies had adopted no formal policy implementing Trump's order that could be reviewed under the Administrative Procedure Act. Members of the three-judge panel, all appointed by Democratic presidents, expressed skepticism saying the administration's position would allow it to avoid judicial review of its efforts to dismantle agencies Congress created so long as it acted "on the down low," as U.S. Circuit Judge Seth Aframe put it. U.S. Circuit Judge Julie Rikelman pointed to evidence presented by 21 Democratic state attorneys general who had sued over the gutting of the agencies showing they were carrying out a policy of effectively shutting themselves down. She noted two agencies eliminated all of their employees after Trump's order. "An agency can't work without people," she said. Rikelman, who like Aframe was appointed by Democratic President Joe Biden, said that ultimately, "the challenge instead was that there was an EO that said the agencies should be closed, which is not up to the administration." The three agencies, which are responsible for mediating labor disputes, supporting minority-owned businesses and preventing homelessness, are among seven that Trump's order had identified. The order called for them to eliminate their non-statutory components and functions to the maximum extent allowed under the law. "The uncontested record in this case shows that defendants functionally shut down three congressionally created agencies by indiscriminately firing all or nearly all of their staff and ceasing to provide programs and services," argued New York Deputy Solicitor General Ester Murdukhayeva. In ruling in favor of the states, McConnell had concluded that the agencies failed to offer any reasonable explanation for why they were being dismantled and that their shuttering ran afoul of the separation of powers principles enshrined in the U.S. Constitution. The administration previously dropped its appeal concerning a fourth agency, the Institute of Museum and Library Services, but continues seeking permission to dismantle the remaining three. The 1st Circuit had earlier [USN:L2N3UY0IX TEXT:"declined to pause"] McConnell's initial preliminary injunction in the case. The three judges on that opinion included Rikelman and U.S. Circuit Judge William Kayatta, who was on the panel that heard Wednesday's appeal. The case is State of Rhode Island v. Trump, 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 26-1070. For the states: Ester Murdukhayeva of the New York Office of the Attorney General For the federal government: Simon Jerome of the U.S. Department of Justice

item.title: Wall St fecha em baixa após Fed elevar juros e sinalizar mais aperto monetário pela frente
item.description: As ações nos EUA fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, depois que o Federal Reserve elevou sua taxa básica de juros pela primeira vez em mais de três anos para combater a inflação persistentemente alta, decorrente da alta vertiginosa dos preços do petróleo bruto durante a guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: As ações nos EUA fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, depois que o Federal Reserve elevou sua taxa básica de juros pela primeira vez em mais de três anos para combater a inflação persistentemente alta, decorrente da alta vertiginosa dos preços do petróleo bruto durante a guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã. Em comunicado divulgado em seguida, o Fed afirmou que sua decisão foi unânime e que é provável que haja mais medidas de aperto monetário no futuro próximo para promover uma queda mais rápida da inflação. “Como amplamente esperado, o Fed elevou as taxas de juros pela primeira vez em mais de três anos”, disse Ryan Detrick, estrategista-chefe de mercado do Carson Group, em Omaha. “A realidade é que o Fed parece unido na luta contra a inflação.” Em sua coletiva de imprensa subsequente, o chair do Fed, Kevin Warsh, disse que a economia dos EUA se fortaleceu desde a última reunião do Fed, mas a tendência da inflação mostrou pouca melhora. “A boa notícia é que o (Fed) não acredita que vários aumentos nos próximos meses terão grande impacto sobre a economia geral, que se mantém sólida”, acrescentou Detrick. “Ao mesmo tempo, a inflação está acima da meta de 2% há cinco anos.” Antes do anúncio do Fed, os três principais índices acionários dos EUA vinham ganhando terreno, com uma recuperação no setor de chips (.SOX) , o que deu vantagem ao Nasdaq, de forte presença do setor de tecnologia. No início do pregão, dados robustos sobre as vendas no varejo sugeriram que os consumidores continuavam gastando, apesar da redução do poder de compra causada pelo aumento dos preços, especialmente na gasolina. A guerra no Oriente Médio se expandiu quando aviões de combate sauditas bombardearam o Iêmen, enquanto combatentes houthis, apoiados pelo Irã, lançaram drones e mísseis contra cidades sauditas — um sinal do alcance ampliado do Irã nesse conflito cada vez mais extenso. Mesmo assim, os preços do petróleo caíram depois que relatos de que a Arábia Saudita estava oferecendo cargas adicionais de petróleo bruto via Omã aliviaram as preocupações com interrupções no abastecimento. O petróleo bruto registrou alta de mais de 20% nas últimas duas semanas e meia. O WTI com vencimento mais curto fechou em queda de 3,2%, e o petróleo Brent caiu 2,7%. O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) recuou 1,21%, para 51.461,78 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) perdeu 0,44%, para 7.552,14 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) teve variação negativa de 0,01%, para 25.978,43 pontos. As ações do setor de tecnologia (.SPLRCT) foram as que mais se valorizaram entre os 11 principais setores do S&P 500, enquanto o setor de energia (.SPNY) , pressionado pela queda nos preços do petróleo bruto, sofreu a maior queda percentual, recuando 3,0%. A Chevron (CVX.N) e a Exxon Mobil (XOM.N) caíram 2,9% e 3,5%, respectivamente, enquanto a Devon Energy (DVN.N) e a ConocoPhillips (COP.N) perderam mais de 5% cada uma. O setor de tecnologia teve um impulso, com as ações de chips (.SOX) subindo 0,6% — seu primeiro ganho significativo desde um apelo conjunto de executivos da área de IA buscando um ritmo mais lento no avanço das capacidades e uma coordenação de segurança em todo o setor. As ações da Robinhood (HOOD.O) tombaram 5,5% depois que o Senado dos EUA não conseguiu aprovar uma legislação abrangente sobre criptomoedas, o que representou um grande golpe para as empresas de ativos digitais. Separadamente, o Departamento de Justiça dos EUA acusou, na terça-feira, dois ex-engenheiros da Robinhood de uso de informação privilegiada e uso indevido de informações confidenciais. As ações da Intel (INTC.O) subiram 4,0% após um relatório indicar que a sul-coreana SK Hynix (000660.KS) estava em negociações com a empresa sobre a fabricação de chips de memória nos Estados Unidos. As ações da SK Hynix , listadas nos EUA, subiram 0,6%. A IBM (IBM.N) registrou queda de 4,4% após a empresa anunciar que a Anderon, sua unidade de chips, assinou um acordo de financiamento com o governo dos EUA. A fabricante de aviões Boeing (BA.N) registrou queda de 3,7% depois que a diretora executiva Kelly Ortberg afirmou que está “demorando mais do que o esperado” para estabilizar a taxa de produção do 737 MAX em 47 aeronaves por mês.

item.title: Shorter-dated US Treasury yields surge in anticipation of another Fed rate hike
item.description: The Federal Reserve increased interest rates for the first time in over three years. Policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter-percentage-point hike by year-end. Shorter-dated U.S. Treasury yields rose after the rate hike announcement. Market bets on a future rate increase at the next meeting ticked higher. Inflation expectations for the next decade remained around 2.3 percent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shorter-dated U.S. Treasury yields rose on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the coming months to control inflation.Two-year Treasury yields extended gains as Fed chief Kevin Warsh spoke and hit 4.738%, their highest level since July 2024. The benchmark 10-year yield turned higher.The decision on the rate increase, which was the Fed's first in over three years, was unanimous.New policy projections showed 16 of 18 policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter-percentage-point hike by the end of this year. Warsh did not submit a rate projection.Also Read: A 25 bps hike: US Federal Reserve raises interest rates for first time since 2023 I'm looking at the two-year here, though, and ... it's coming back up higher here. So, maybe it helps the long end a little bit, but the front end's still worried about another hike later this year, and then who knows what for 2027, said JP Powers, chief investment officer at RWA Wealth Partners in Boston.Market bets on a rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in late October ticked higher to 56.5% from 54% prior to the hike, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.The two-year U.S. Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was last up 5.1 basis points at 4.715%.Also Read:US Fed chair Kevin Warsh explains why the Federal Reserve raised interest ratesThe yield on the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury note was last down 0.2 basis points at 4.994% after briefly turning higher.The yield on the 30-year bond fell 2.5 basis points to 5.338%.A closely watched part of the U.S. Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes, seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 27.5 basis points, the flattest since June 30.The breakeven rate on five-year U.S. Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) was last at 2.366% after closing at 2.417% on Tuesday.The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate was last at 2.344%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.3% a year for the next decade.

item.title: Revolut diz não ter recebido reivindicação direta sobre suposta violação de dados
item.description: A Revolut não teve nenhum contato direto nem recebeu qualquer exigência do grupo que assumiu a responsabilidade por uma violação de dados da companhia, informou um porta-voz da empresa à Reuters nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Revolut não teve nenhum contato direto nem recebeu qualquer exigência do grupo que assumiu a responsabilidade por uma violação de dados da companhia, informou um porta-voz da empresa à Reuters nesta quarta-feira. O Financial Times publicou mais cedo que hackers que assumiram a responsabilidade por uma violação de dados da empresa ameaçaram vender registros confidenciais de centenas de clientes a outros grupos criminosos, a menos que a Revolut pagasse um resgate de US$3 milhões em até 24 horas. A infraestrutura principal, os bancos de dados e as contas dos clientes da Revolut não foram invadidos, disse uma fonte a par do assunto. A violação teria afetado cerca de 680 clientes, segundo a fonte. O grupo, que se autodenomina “iamnotavillain”, publicou o ultimato online na tarde desta quarta-feira ao lado de um relógio de contagem regressiva digital, segundo a reportagem do jornal. O grupo disse ao jornal que estava usando o site para apresentar suas exigências pela primeira vez e que não havia havido nenhuma negociação com a Revolut. A Revolut informou no sábado que informações confidenciais de clientes foram divulgadas a terceiros não autorizados após ter recebido solicitações fraudulentas provenientes de um domínio de email de uma agência governamental legítima. (Por Gnaneshwar Rajan e Preetika Parashuraman)

item.title: Mets place Robert Stock on IL, recall Xzavion Curry to face Orioles
item.description: The New York Mets placed right-handers Robert Stock and Daniel Duarte on the 15-day injured list, while right-hander Xzavion Curry was recalled to start Wednesday night against the Baltimore Orioles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Mets placed right-handers Robert Stock and Daniel Duarte on the 15-day injured list, while right-hander Xzavion Curry was recalled to start Wednesday night against the Baltimore Orioles. The Mets also recalled left-hander Jefry Yan as they try to move out of last place in the National League East with less than two weeks remaining in the regular season. Stock, 36, last pitched Wednesday when he allowed three runs over four innings in a no-decision against the Miami Marlins in a 15-14 win and was expected to return to the mound against the Orioles. Stock was placed on the IL with numbness in his fingers and saw his season come to an end after going 1-3 with a 5.93 ERA in eight appearances (seven starts). Duarte, 29, is dealing with a left hamstring strain and finishes his season 2-0 with a 2.12 ERA in 24 relief appearances. Curry, 28, had eight relief appearances with the Mets earlier this season and delivered a 3.44 ERA. Yan, 30, made his major league debut Aug. 5 and went 1-1 with a 5.68 ERA in 13 relief appearances. --Field Level Media

item.title: India cuts windfall tax on export of petrol, diesel, aviation fuel
item.description: India has lowered windfall taxes on exports of petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel with immediate effect, according to a government order issued late on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India has lowered windfall taxes on exports of petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel with immediate effect, according to a government order issued late on Wednesday. Here are more details from the order The duty on diesel exports has been cut to 20 rupees per litre from 25 rupees earlier. The levy on export of petrol been cut to 0.5 rupees per litre from 1.5 rupees earlier. The tax on aviation turbine fuel has been set at 15 rupees per litre from 19 rupees earlier.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em queda após Fed elevar juro e sinalizar mais aperto
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quarta-feira, renovando mínima da sessão à tarde, após o banco central dos Estados Unidos elevar a taxa básica de juros na maior economia do mundo e sinalizar mais uma alta neste ano.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quarta-feira, renovando mínima da sessão à tarde, após o banco central dos Estados Unidos elevar a taxa básica de juros na maior economia do mundo e sinalizar mais uma alta neste ano. Índice de referência do mercado acionário, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) recuou 0,51%, a 185.547,66 pontos, após marcar 186.738,25 na máxima e 184.753,98 na mínima do dia. O volume financeiro somou R$72,48 bilhões, em pregão também marcado por vencimento de opções sobre o Ibovespa. A B3 fechou com investidores na expectativa da decisão do Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) do Banco Central, com as [USN:L6N4560N2 TEXT:"apostas"] indicando redução da taxa Selic de 14% para 13,75% ao ano. "A bolsa passou o dia refém da 'superquarta' e o pregão foi mais de posicionamento do que de convicção", afirmou o CEO da Gravus Capital, Ricardo Trevisan. Nos EUA, no meio da tarde, o Federal Reserve promoveu o primeiro [USN:S0N43T00Y TEXT:"aperto monetário"] desde 2023 ao elevar a taxa básica de juros overnight em 0,25 ponto percentual, para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%, em decisão unânime. Novas projeções também mostraram que 16 autoridades do Fed preveem pelo menos mais um aumento de 0,25 ponto até o final deste ano, enquanto duas estimam estabilidade. Na entrevista à imprensa após o anúncio da decisão, o chair do Fed, Kevin Warsh, [USN:L6N45814D TEXT:"afirmou"] que a economia dos EUA se fortaleceu desde junho, enquanto as tendências da inflação mostraram pouca melhora. "A estabilidade dos preços vem sendo o problema há mais de cinco anos e meio", afirmou. Em Wall Street, o S&P 500 (.SPX) fechou com declínio de 0,45%, enquanto o rendimento do título de 10 anos do Tesouro dos EUA marcava 5,0205% no final do dia, de 4,996% na véspera. De acordo com Trevisan, a alta de 0,25 ponto estava no preço e havia expectativa de uma sinalização de um ciclo mais longo de aperto. Mas o comunicado foi firme ao falar em acelerar o retorno da inflação à meta, ressaltou. Ele destacou que a decisão ocorre no mesmo dia em que o Copom deve cortar a Selic, encolhendo o diferencial de juros entre os dois países. "Para o investidor estrangeiro, parte da vantagem de manter recursos em reais desaparece, justamente às vésperas de uma eleição decisiva e com o crédito corporativo sob estresse", afirmou. "Minha leitura é que o Copom perde espaço para acelerar o ciclo e deve seguir decidindo reunião a reunião, com muita cautela na comunicação", acrescentou. Para Trevisan, o que vai definir o pregão de quinta-feira na B3 não é o corte da Selic, e sim o comunicado. "Eu espero um Banco Central cauteloso, sem se comprometer com a continuidade do ciclo." Dados atualizados da B3 mostraram mais um dia com saída líquida das ações brasileiras. Até o dia 14, o saldo de capital externo estava positivo em R$7 bilhões em setembro. Na conta até o dia 11, eram R$7,3 bilhões. DESTAQUES PETROBRAS PN recuou 3,53% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) perdeu 4,27%, acompanhando o declínio dos preços do petróleo no exterior, onde o barril sob o contrato Brent fechou em baixa de 2,69%, a US$105,83, pressionando também outras petrolíferas na B3. BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) fechou em alta de 3,04%, ganhando fôlego na segunda etapa do pregão, em dia misto para o setor no Ibovespa. ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN caiu 0,12%, BRADESCO PN encerrou com variação positiva de 0,05% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT recuou 0,96%. NUBANK (NU.N) , que é listado nos EUA, recuou 2,68%, com relatório do Itaú BBA cortando a recomendação das ações de "outperform" para "market perform". VALE ON (VALE3.SA) caiu 2,14%, em pregão de oscilação modesta dos futuros do [USN:L6N4580OQ TEXT:"minério de ferro"] na China, onde o contrato mais negociado na Bolsa de Commodities de Dalian encerrou o pregão diurno com alta de 0,14%. MAGAZINE LUIZA ON (MGLU3.SA) avançou 6,64%, em sessão positiva também para ações de outros varejistas, com ASSAÍ ON (ASAI3.SA) subindo 4,66% e LOJAS RENNER ON (LREN3.SA) valorizando-se 3,14%, endossadas pelo alívio nas taxas dos DIs com prazos mais longos e expectativa de novo alívio monetário no Brasil. BRASKEM PNA , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, desabou 15,17%, após analistas do UBS BB cortarem a recomendação das ações para venda, reduzindo o preço-alvo de R$10,50 para R$3,75. Os analistas afirmaram que continuam sem enxergar uma saída fácil para o cenário atual da companhia. O jornal Valor Econômico também reportou que a petroquímica enviou aos credores termos mais detalhados para sua reestruturação financeira e incorporou a previsão de deságio (“haircut”) na dívida.

item.title: Israel, Morocco agree to upgrade diplomatic ties, Israeli government says
item.description: The foreign ministers of Israel and Morocco agreed to upgrade diplomatic ties and open embassies and appoint ambassadors in both countries, according to a statement on Wednesday by the official Israeli government account in Arabic on X.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The foreign ministers of Israel and Morocco agreed to upgrade diplomatic ties and open embassies and appoint ambassadors in both countries, according to a statement on Wednesday by the official Israeli government account in Arabic on X. Morocco was one of four Arab countries - along with the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Sudan - to move towards normalizing relations with Israel in 2020 under U.S.-engineered accords.
